content_voiceover: Now let's talk about the reagents used in the direct Coombs test, because knowing mono-specific versus poly-specific AHG is a classic exam point. AHG stands for anti-human globulin. Poly-specific AHG contains both anti-IgG and anti-C3d antibodies combined into a single reagent — so a positive result just tells you the red cells are coated with either IgG, complement, or both, without telling you which. Mono-specific AHG reagents are separate — one tube contains only anti-IgG, another contains only anti-C3d, so if you run both mono-specific reagents you can tell exactly which coating is present. This can be done either by the card method, called gel card testing, or by the traditional tube method, where you can see the anti-C3d, anti-IgG, and combined anti-IgG-plus-anti-C3d reagent bottles side by side. In practice, most labs run mono-specific IgG and C3d and a control together on one card, so you get IgG, C3d, and control results simultaneously without needing to run poly-specific separately every time. Being able to distinguish IgG-only, complement-only, or combined coating patterns is essential because, as we'll see, that pattern actually helps classify the type of immune hemolytic anemia.
keypoints: AHG stands for anti-human globulin; poly-specific AHG contains both anti-IgG and anti-C3d in one reagent.
Mono-specific AHG reagents test anti-IgG and anti-C3d separately, allowing you to identify which one coats the RBC.
Testing can be performed by the gel card method or the traditional tube method.
The IgG versus C3d coating pattern helps classify the subtype of immune hemolytic anemia.
keypoint_voiceover: Remember, AHG means anti-human globulin. Poly-specific AHG combines anti-IgG and anti-C3d into one reagent, so a positive result doesn't tell you which is present. Mono-specific AHG separates them into individual anti-IgG and anti-C3d reagents, letting you pinpoint exactly what's coating the red cells. This can be tested by gel card or tube method. Why does this matter? Because the specific pattern of IgG versus complement coating helps you classify which type of immune hemolytic anemia you're dealing with.
